newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes end the week on down side, grades even.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes end the week on down side, grades even.

text.p: Prices for U.S. crudes decreased Friday on continued pressure generated by bearish inventory data, though losses were less severe than in morning activity, traders said.

Outrights spent all session on the down side, due to Thursday's release of stock numbers showing distillate stocks building at the same time warm weather swept across the key heating oil belt in the Northeast United States.
February West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended around 10 cents lower at $25.50-60 a barrel, cutting declines in half from earlier, while Feb/March WTI closed out around 60 cts.
Domestic grades failed to budge from ranges established in the morning, trading most fervently in the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James where barrels sold at 37-43 cts over the WTI/Cushing.
Refiner demand remained muted for domestic and foreign barrels, though arbitrage openings continued to stay wide.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire ended the week at a 26-30 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing, steady from Thursday, but higher from earlier trades under a 25 cts premium.
Midland/WTI talked at steady to the WTI marker, again unchanged with little action noted.
Sour grades saw barrels of West Texas Sour/Midland sell between a $1.42-$1.40 discount to the WTI/Cushing, within the wider ranges seen yesterday.
Feb Postings Plus at Cushing sold at weaker levels between $2.42-44, some 5 cts lower than previously confirmed.
